question_put_to_a_human: What are chapters 735 through 744 about, in one sentence? Put to a human before this file was written, as it has been put before every writer since 595. No human has answered it for any block from 595 onward. No writer answers it for them. It is recorded here unanswered and it stays a writer's to leave open until somebody answers it.
family: THE FAMILY FOR THIS BLOCK IS DECLARED BEFORE ANY CHAPTER EXISTS AND IT IS A WRITER'S, NOT A HUMAN'S. **A number that is right, and a person who will not make it fit.** Ten chapters, five standing figures and one young man given one chapter, and in each chapter there is a figure that does not agree with the thing it is supposed to be measuring, and somebody is on hand who could make it agree, and does not. The ten: six things on a gas envelope with five of them finished and not one crossed off, and no pencil in the house to cross one. Three chalk marks on the back of a gate where one of the three is an inch out. Four lines on an invoice pad with a thing on one of them. Six pads on a fridge with two of them crossed and three acts done between them. Three lines of paper with nothing on them under any of them and nothing saying what anything weighs or costs. Two lists on one piece of paper that cannot be laid side by side. A quarter inch that turns out to be two numbers. Four rooms on a slip and three things on the back of it. Four door frames and three doors on one landing. Three lines of paper put in a drawer on top of the hammer and the screwdriver that would do them.
family_measured_against_the_prose_after_: The first draft of this file said three of the figures change, three are said out loud for the first time, four are not spoken, and that nothing is put right. The prose does not bear that out and the prose wins, so the file now says what the ten chapters do. **Three figures change:** 0736 one chalk mark comes off a gate and becomes no mark at all, 0738 three acts are counted out loud where a reader would expect two pads crossed, and 0741 one quarter inch becomes two numbers that are both right. **Four figures are said out loud to another person for the first time in their own account:** five in 0735, three in 0738, the out-of-square finding in 0741, and the figure for four rooms in 0742. **Three things are put right and one is not:** the drip into the bowl at number twelve stops in 0735, a wrong chalk mark comes off a gate in 0736, a strip of ply starts standing against a shed edge in 0744, and the freeholder still does not come.
why_not_no_family_again: 0054 took no family and gave its reason in its own band file, that thirteen spreads of one shape are the defect. That reason holds for a spread and it does not hold twice running for the absence of one. Two blocks of no family is a shape of its own, and a reader given ten standalone scenes and then ten more is being told the same thing about this borough twice in a row. So this block takes a family, and the family is a count that will not be made to fit, which is the one shape available in the standing objects and is not one of the fourteen spent ones.

family_tested_against_every_spent_family.595_604_a_small_thing_went_nowhere: Not this. Here three figures change and four are spoken. A small thing going nowhere has no figure in it that anybody could correct.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.605_614_carried_a_thing_they_could_not_p: Not this. Nothing is carried between two people in the ten. Where a thing is carried it is carried once, by the person it belongs to, across her own yard.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.615_624_told_a_thing_they_could_not_plac: Not this. Nothing is told as news. Four figures are spoken and every one of them is spoken to somebody who already knows the work: five things finished to a sister, a count of acts to a woman who does the shopping, two numbers to a lad with a van, a price to the woman who books it.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.625_634_decided_something_and_was_asked_: Not this. Nobody is asked why and gives a reason as the engine of a scene. A woman at twelve is asked what is on the other side of a piece of paper and tells her sister it is a list of rooms she wrote herself, which is information and not a justification.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.635_644_brought_a_thing_and_somebody_els: Not this. Nobody lies. Five of the ten turns are refusals and not one of them needs a false sentence.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.645_654_a_woman_wrote_and_the_paper_left: Close enough to test hard and it does not touch. That family is about paper leaving a house in an order nobody can explain. No paper leaves any house in the ten. The gas envelope at number twelve is a document that has stayed in this kitchen for months and 0740 turns on the fact that nobody will turn it over, which is the opposite engine: the document is kept, and the reason it is kept is that nobody wants it compared with the other side of it.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.655_664_a_brush_carried_through_by_three: Not this. No object passes from one person to another anywhere in the ten. The brush on the runner at number twelve is stepped over in 0735 and 0740 and not picked up. The brush in the bag in the drawer at the unit is not taken out in 0741 when the drawer is opened, and the chapter says so in as many words.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.665_674_a_room_she_will_not_sit_in_and_a: Not this, and this is the family most likely to be mistaken for it. The front room at number twelve and the propped gate at number twelve are standing states and neither is the family here. The front room is not entered in any of the ten. The gate is not shut, latched, propped or looked at in any of the ten. Neither of those is a chapter.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.675_684_a_parcel_that_came_back_with_a_s: Not this. The taped box on the table at number twelve stays taped, keeps its cloth over it, and is not the subject of any chapter. It is on the table in 0735 and 0740 as furniture and it does not move in either.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.685_694_a_step_ladder_round_four_houses_: Not this. The ladder at number twelve stays folded under the front window with tape on the second rail and chalk on the third. 0740 names why it cannot go anywhere and there is no fifth ladder in the ten.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.695_704_work_put_off_to_a_season_with_a_: Not this. Nothing is put off to a season. Four things are actually done in the ten: a washer goes into a bath tap, a wrong chalk mark comes off a gate, a mirror comes off a wall and goes into a van, and a strip of ply starts standing against a shed edge.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.705_714_water_coming_and_a_bowl_emptied_: The nearest one, and it is not dodged. 0735 stops the drip into the white bowl under the bath tap and puts the bowl on the shelf above the sink. That is a consequence of a repair she makes with her own hands and it happens once. The cistern four streets away still weeps and is not touched. The water family is not the family here and the bowl is not in the other nine.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.715_724_a_call_to_a_house_where_the_pers: Not this. There is no telephone in this block. No bell rings, no receiver is lifted, no number is read out, no call is made and no message is left. The telephone and the machine at number twelve stand on the low table in the front room and are not touched. The telephone class does not appear at all in the ten, which is stricter than the one appearance the prompt allowed.
family_tested_against_every_spent_family.725_734_no_family_ten_scenes_each_standi: This is the block this one is written against, and the finding is that taking none twice is a shape of its own. This block takes a family and then breaks it three times: in 0736 a figure comes off a gate and into the air, in 0738 a count of three acts is said out loud where a reader would expect two pads crossed, and in 0741 the figure a man has carried for four months turns out to be two numbers, which is the family failing at its own arithmetic.

cards.0735: A woman of seventy-eight gets the handle off her own bath tap at number twelve on Monday the twentieth of June, gets a scratch on the chrome with pliers she should not have used, marks that this is the first time off and that it will not be the last, lets her sister take the cloth on the bathroom sill and stops her at the door frame, puts a washer in with an adjustable and hears the drip stop, says the word five out loud to somebody for the first time in her life, and puts the bowl on the shelf above the sink and leaves the ring on the tiles.
cards.0736: A man in his early forties lays his own tape along the top of a six foot run at his unit on Thursday the twenty-third of June and gets a quarter inch as he always does, tells a man who has come about the gates what true means and what the quarter inch is out loud, finds three chalk marks on the back of one gate and that one of them is wrong, rubs that one out with his thumb and leaves the other two.
cards.0737: A woman in her late forties puts a knee under a box that has sat behind her own bench at the lock-up since October on Monday the twenty-seventh of June and feels the contents of it shift and settle, finds the lid is not nailed and one corner stands an inch, does not open it, tells the man with keys it is not heavy and is not going to be found out, rules two more lines on the pad and writes nothing on either, and pushes the rags flat so the corner stands where she can see which way the lid folds over on.
cards.0738: A woman in her late fifties reads the six pads on her own fridge at number nine on Saturday the second of July, takes the woman who has been going to the shop for her at the front door, lets her read all six aloud, puts the first one down on the table and admits she cannot account for it being crossed twice, refuses her the fifth pad outright, counts three acts out loud where a reader would expect two pads crossed, and lets the six go back on the fridge with the first one at the bottom of them and does not put it back on top.
cards.0739: A woman in her early thirties reads the three lines on her own paper out loud at number ten on Tuesday the fifth of July because a boy is over the fence for a ball, gets as far as the third and stops, tells him that a gate which will not shut is either the gate or the frame and one of them is out, gives him the ball back over the fence, and puts the paper face down on her own table.
cards.0740: A woman of seventy-eight has her sister in the kitchen at number twelve on Friday the eighth of July over a gas envelope with six things in her own pencil on the back of it and somebody else's list of rooms on the front with the top corner gone off it by tape, refuses her sister's offer to copy the six onto a fresh sheet with a pencil brought from her own house on the ground that a copy of six things is seven things and she has never been able to say which six, refuses her the second thing as well, does not say whose the other list is, and does not turn the envelope over.
cards.0741: A man in his early forties opens the drawer under his own bench at the unit on Tuesday the twelfth of July for the first time since November, takes out a square and leaves the bag with the brush in it shut on the bottom of the drawer, puts the square across the face of a six foot run and finds the frame true, puts the tape along the top of it and gets six foot and a quarter inch, puts the tape along the bottom of it and gets six foot, says both out loud to a lad with a van in one sentence, and puts the square back without writing either number down.
cards.0742: A woman in her late forties is at the lock-up on Friday the fifteenth of July when a woman who books work brings an address that names four rooms where her own list says three things, asks twice whether the fourth is a room or a landing, is told it is a room and that it is empty, asks for the figure for four rooms twice and is given it twice and neither writing goes anywhere, rules one line on the pad and puts the date on it and nothing else, and puts the slip in her coat.
cards.0743: A man in his late twenties goes up a turning stair in a house two streets back from the ring road on Wednesday the twentieth of July to get a sideboard down for a clearance that is four rooms and three things, counts four door frames where there are three doors and tells the woman he is working for so, gets the sideboard down in two goes alone, takes a mirror off the landing wall because it fouls the turn and is told it is not the woman's to give, puts it in the back of his van facing forward, and puts nothing on the bare patch of wall it came off.
cards.0744: A woman in her early thirties carries a ply offcut off the wall and stands it against the shed at number ten on Saturday the twenty-third of July and does not nail it, is offered her own three lines of paper for her sister's table and says no because that would make it her sister's job, tells her sister she will put the paper in the drawer and does not do it in front of her, and puts it into the drawer under her own worktop with the hammer and the screwdriver after her sister has gone and shuts the drawer.

canon_scenes_turned_away_from.0735: Turns away from 0705, the woman of seventy-eight emptying a bowl and speaking to a woman at the back door about a meter who does not come in. There is no bowl emptied, no meter and no woman at the door in 0735. There is a bath tap, a washer cut from a roll of sheet, and a sister stopped at a door frame. The standing fact that she will not have anybody near the tap is honoured by keeping the sister in the passage for the whole of the work. It also turns away from the cistern weeping at the far side of a joist four streets away, which is not touched and not mentioned.
canon_scenes_turned_away_from.0736: Turns away from 0706 and 0718, the man at the unit with the run a quarter inch out, the borrowed ladder and the water under a bath tap. No ladder is borrowed and no water is mentioned. 0736 is the same figure run in the other direction: he has said the quarter inch aloud before, to the man at the bench opposite in a yard in the spring, and 0736 says so in the body rather than claiming a first.
canon_scenes_turned_away_from.0737: Turns away from 0712, the lock-up with a bag of rags and somebody else's blanket in it and a man at the lock-up and a taped box with a bagged corner. No rag is moved to anywhere in 0737 and the blanket is not touched. What moves is the box, by half an inch, from underneath.
canon_scenes_turned_away_from.0738: Turns away from 0708, number nine with a scrubbing bucket and a stool looked at and a sister spoken to at the door about felt and about a dripping tap. 0738 has no sister, no felt, no tap and no bucket, and the person at the door is the woman who does the shopping. Different door, different person, different reason.
canon_scenes_turned_away_from.0739: Turns away from 0720, the table at number ten with the paper out and a telephone left ringing, and from 0692, the paper folded into the drawer. Nothing rings and the paper is on the table. 0739 is the chapter in which the three lines are read out loud, which no earlier chapter does.
canon_scenes_turned_away_from.0740: Turns away from 0705 again and from 0665, the writing of the room list on the front of the envelope. 0740 writes nothing. It turns away from 0649 and 0653 as well, where the envelope is turned over: **the envelope is not turned over anywhere in 0740, the list on the front is somebody else's and is never named as anybody's, no room on it is read out, and the corner is gone because tape took it off rather than because tape covers it. Canon disagrees with itself about whose hand the front of that envelope carries, so the chapter asserts nothing about it, and a later writer may not either without a ruling.**
canon_scenes_turned_away_from.0741: Turns away from 0711, the cottage lane with the posts, and from 0693, the unit with the quarter inch. The cottage is not in this chapter. The quarter inch is measured with a square along the face and with the tape along the top and then along the bottom, and the finding is a frame out of square rather than a length out, which is a different number from the one 0736 carries and does not contradict it. It also turns away from the brush chapters 0655 to 0664: the drawer under the bench is opened and the bag with the brush in it stays shut and the chapter says so.
canon_scenes_turned_away_from.0742: Turns away from 0714, the woman booking work with a slip in her hand, and from 0732, the van doors shut and tried at the lock-up. There is no van and no door shut in 0742 and no clearing done; it is a slip with an address on it and a figure given aloud in a lock-up.
canon_scenes_turned_away_from.0743: Turns away from 0670, a telephone lifted in a house off the ring road, and from 0719, the same house with a bell in a room at the back. There is no telephone and no bell in 0743 and nothing rings. It also turns away from 0712: the house is somebody else's and he is there for a sideboard on a stair, not for a landing answer.
canon_scenes_turned_away_from.0744: Turns away from 0729, the yard at number ten with ply tried and a line re-pegged, and from 0734, the tools put into the drawer with the paper left out on the table. 0744 is the chapter in which the paper goes into the drawer with the tools, and it says in the body that she is doing the opposite of what she did before and gives the reason.
canon_scenes_turned_away_from.rule: No chapter re-stages a canon scene about a ladder, hatch, cistern, ballcock, coal shed, browse, brush or telephone ringing. Four step ladders on the page and no fifth appears in the ten. The travelling one stays folded at number twelve. The fixed four rungs by the hatch, the fibreglass one in the lamp man's van and the folded one in a semi back room are untouched. The two-tread step stool in the unit corner is not a ladder and is not used as one. The brush on the passage runner at number twelve is stepped over twice and not moved. The brush in the bag in the drawer at the unit is not taken out. The coal shed door is not opened in any of the ten. The coal shed is shut with the padlock open in the hasp and the key on its hook behind the back door, as at 0734.

movement: Nothing is rescued. The freeholder does not arrive. No plate is unscrewed and no wire is spliced and nobody rings through to anyone who can act. The ladder is not opened and no room is painted. The box behind the bench is not opened. The drawer with leads and screws is not opened. The hall line on the invoice pad stays empty. The ninety yards stay unwalked. What changes in the ten: a washer goes into a bath tap at number twelve and the bowl comes off the floor; one wrong chalk mark is rubbed off a gate; a box under rags shifts half an inch and one corner of its lid stands up; two empty lines are ruled on an invoice pad; a woman counts three acts out loud where a reader expects two pads crossed; a woman at nine refuses a copy of six things and does not turn a piece of paper over; a drawer under a bench is opened and a bag inside it stays shut; a frame a quarter inch out at the top and square at the bottom turns out to be out of square the whole way along; an address with four rooms is priced at four; a mirror comes off a wall and goes into a van; a ply offcut is stood against a shed and not nailed; a piece of paper with three lines on it goes into a drawer with the hammer and the screwdriver.
door_meetings: Three of the ten have somebody come to a door. 0735 a sister at the back door and then a door frame of a bathroom, 0738 the woman who does the shopping at the front door of number nine, 0740 a sister at the front door of number twelve, 0744 a sister at the gate of number ten, and 0742 a woman who books work at the doors of the lock-up. **The same two people at the same door happens in no two chapters out of ten.** The two sisters at number twelve are at two different doors on two different days and speak in two different rooms. The sister at number nine and the sister at number ten are a different figure and are not compared to each other anywhere in the ten.
closing_images: Ten different ones, deliberately. A pale ring on bathroom tiles. A clean patch on the back of a gate. The corner of a box lid standing up out of rags under a light. A knotted bag by the back door. A folded paper face down on a table. A piece of paper not turned over. A drawer shut on a bag and a brush. A wall behind a bench with a figure rubbed off it. A bare patch on a landing wall with nothing put on it. A hand coming off a drawer front and a back door shutting true. **No gesture is inverted or repeated in more than two chapters, and no chapter ends on a piece of paper lying flat in a stated order.**

prohibitions_honoured.day_count_census: **First half, numeral with a unit.** Numeral plus seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months or years: **zero** across the ten, in body, dateline, opening and closing. **Second half, every numeral of any size.** The only numerals in the ten files are the chapter number in each title line and the year in each dateline. read_back: The ten were given to a second reader with eight canon chapters and the fourteen points carried from 0053, and thirty findings came back. **Twenty-nine were fixed in the prose and every card in this file was then corrected to the prose.** The largest were: 0740 had been built on a misreading of the gas envelope and was rewritten from the ground, since the list on the front is her own and the envelope is never turned over; 0741's central finding did not add up arithmetically and was rebuilt as a frame out of square; 0735 contradicted itself about which drawer the pen is in; 0736 claimed a first time in a man's life that chapter 0706 had already spent; 0742's caps block had the figure going the wrong way; 0743's caps block put a mirror in two places; 0738's caps block asserted a refusal the body does not stage. Four were left standing and recorded rather than repaired: the box behind the bench at the lock-up is in the van in chapter 0712 and behind the bench in the prompt and in this block, and the conflict is older than this block and is not this writer's to settle; the three and a half inches of tape were cut out of 0739 rather than left; the phrase did not tell you a number with the same small verb three times is gone; and the kitchen inventory paragraphs of 0735 and 0740 were rewritten apart from each other. **Where prose and card disagreed the file was corrected to the chapter.**
